title: AI Pavement Crack Analysis
summary: Developed a deep learning algorithm that detects pavement cracks at the pixel level and measures each crack's direction (horizontal or vertical), length and width.
highlights: Built a new training set of Korean road cracks and trained DeepCrack (based on SegNet)
Added crack width to the ground truth so the model detects width as well
Trained horizontal and vertical cracks separately and computed length and width per crack, assuming 1 px = 1 mm

title: Integrated, Accelerated Camera-Based Vehicle Vision Signal Processing
summary: Parallelized a road detection algorithm with NVIDIA CUDA and achieved real-time processing on an embedded board (Jetson TK1).
highlights: Profiled the compute bottlenecks of CPU-based road detection and moved them to CUDA parallel processing
Measured and validated on a Jetson TK1 board

metrics.label: Average processing speed, CPU vs GPU

title: Real-Time License Plate Detection
role: Recognition algorithm research and development (60% contribution)
summary: Developed an algorithm that detects and reads the plates of vehicles moving under 30 km/h in real time.
highlights: Classified plates into types by their visual features, then recognized each type separately
Works on both old and new Korean plate formats

title: Real-Time Road Region Extraction for Front-Facing Vehicle Cameras
summary: Researched an algorithm that extracts the road region in real time on highways, national roads and busy city streets. Published at ISVC'15.
highlights: Detected road candidate regions using the S channel of the HSV color space
Refined the road boundary by correcting false detections with edge information

title: Effective Multi-Object Segmentation and Tracking with Video Signal Processing
subtitle: Blind-spot vehicle detection · Front pedestrian detection
summary: Researched algorithms that detect vehicles in the driver's blind spot and pedestrians ahead, and warn of danger.
highlights: Detected blind-spot vehicles with learned vehicle features and corrected false candidate regions
Proposed a pedestrian detector that addresses HOG's limits with a wavelet transform

title: Short-Range Visible Light Communication Convergence Technology (Year 3)
summary: Analyzed the visible light communication standard (IEEE 802.15.7) and built an H.264/AVC player for video transmission.
highlights: Analyzed the TX/RX physical layers, LED interface, positioning and identification structures of IEEE 802.15.7
Developed an H.264/AVC-based encoder and an MPEG-4-based decoder

subtitle: Hiding text inside images
summary: Converts text to binary, hides it in the least significant bits of each pixel's R, G and B values, and restores it. The output looks identical to the original and has the same file size.

title: Smarter CCTV with Motion Detection and Face DNA
role: Face recognition and face-DNA algorithms (60% contribution)
summary: A CCTV program that records and alerts the user's phone only when motion is detected and an unregistered face appears, reducing wasteful recording and slow after-the-fact response.
highlights: Pipeline: motion detection → face detection → face data (DNA) comparison
Unregistered faces trigger video and photo upload to the web and phone, plus an alert

title: Augmented Driving System (ADS) for Richer Driver Information
role: Vehicle detection, gesture recognition and lane detection (50% contribution)
summary: A driver-assistance interface that uses a single camera to detect the distance to the car ahead, lanes and traffic signs, shows them on a HUD, and is controlled by voice and gestures.
highlights: Vehicle detection and distance, license plate detection, lane departure warning, traffic sign recognition
HUD interface: call it by voice, choose menus by gesture
One paper at a Korean academic conference

metrics.label: Recognition rate for signs, lanes and following distance (road test)
